thread.title: Apple buoys Silicon Valley stocks, Lumentum soars as Wall St volatility continues

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Apple buoys Silicon Valley stocks, Lumentum soars as Wall St volatility continues
text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 6, 2018, 1:42pm PST Updated Feb 6, 2018, 2:39pm PST The Bloomberg Silicon Valley Technology index closed up 2.94 percent on Tuesday — regaining much of its decline from Monday's global stocks selloff — amid another wild day on Wall Street. All 13 of the companies on the index of Silicon Valley's largest technology stocks were up Tuesday. They were led by the biggest of them all, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), with the Cupertino-based iPhone maker rising 3.67 percent. Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) gained 3.15 percent. Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO) closed up 2.87 percent and Oracle Corp. (NYSE: ORCL) rose 2.08 percent. Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) climbed 1.46 percent. Reports of higher iPhone components sales also catapulted shares of Milpitas-based Apple supplier Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE) 21.24 percent higher on Tuesday. Reporting second-quarter earnings, the company said it shipped more than $200 million worth of 3-D sensing lasers to a customer that several analysts identified as Apple, Reuters reported . Lumentum's quarterly revenue soared 52 percent to $404.6 million in the quarter. Among all Silicon Valley stocks, the other best performers on Tuesday were: Infinera Corp. (NASDAQ:INFN) closed up 9.28 percent. The optical networking company reports quarterly earnings tomorrow . Fortinet (NASDAQ: FTNT) jumped 6.18 percent after beating fourth-quarter earnings expectations . Cypress Semiconductor Corp. (NASDAQ: CY) bounced 5.22 percent. The San Jose-based chipmaker was one of the hardest-hit Bay Area stocks in yesterday's stock-market downturn, but investors appear to be soothed Tuesday after CEO Hassane El-Khoury told CNBC's Jim Cramer that the company is bullish on its 2018 outlook . Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA), another chipmaker that was pummeled on Monday, recovered and closed up 5.56 percent on Tuesday. The worst performers among Silicon Valley's publicly traded companies: SunPower Corp. ( NASDAQ: SPWR) dropped 2.08 percent, the day after it was announced that it would sell the renewable energy joint venture it co-owns with Arizona's First Solar (NASDAQ: FSLR) in a below-market price sale to a Swiss private equity firm. Hard-drive maker Seagate Technology (NASDAQ: STX) slipped 1.95 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average plummeted 567 points in early trading Monday, then rallied and ultimately closed up 567 points, or 2.33 percent. The S&P 500 closed up 1.74 percent. The Nasdaq gained 2.13 percent. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 6, 2018, 1:42pm PST Updated Feb 6, 2018, 2:39pm PST Related Content
